testName: Air Brakes Test #1 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of an air brake system?
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: the service brake system, the parking brake system, and the emergency brake system.

questions.question: If the low pressure warning signal turns on while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Exit the road and park as soon as safely possible.
Stop where you are and park.
Turn on hazard lights and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the road and park as soon as safely possible.
questions.explanation: If the low pressure warning signal turns on, safely exit the road and park your vehicle as soon as possible. Low air pressure means your brakes may not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: Where must the ABS malfunction lamp be located on a dolly with ABS?
questions.explanation: A dolly with ABS must have a yellow malfunction lamp on its left side.

questions.question: What happens when only the tractor has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS)?

options.text: The brakes do not work as well without ABS.

questions.explanation: When only the tractor has ABS, the risk of jackknifing is reduced. The driver can keep steering control. If only the trailer has ABS, the trailer is less likely to swing to one side.

questions.question: What color are ABS malfunction lamps?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow malfunction lamps.

questions.question: In a static leakage test, what is the maximum air leakage rate for a double combination vehicle?
questions.explanation: During a static leakage test on a double combination vehicle, air leakage should not exceed 3 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster, the vehicle should not be driven because something needs repair.

questions.question: When you push the brake pedal in an air brake system, what happens?

options.text: The low pressure warning light turns on.
The low pressure warning light turns off.

questions.explanation: When you push the brake pedal, air pressure activates an electric switch. This switch turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor control?

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks.
The temperature of air pumped into the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.

questions.question: What can happen if you use the parking brake in very wet weather when it is freezing?

options.text: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
The brakes may suddenly release by themselves.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
questions.explanation: In very wet weather below freezing, the parking brake can freeze. This prevents the vehicle from moving.

questions.question: If spring brakes are activated, what should you never do?

options.text: Release air from the storage tanks.
Open the door to the cab.

questions.explanation: Never push the brake pedal when spring brakes are activated. Using both springs and air pressure together can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What can be found in the air entering air storage tanks?
questions.explanation: Air entering storage tanks in an air brake system contains water and compressor oil. These materials can damage the braking system. Tanks have drain valves to remove them.

questions.question: How do you remove water and compressor oil from an air storage tank?

options.text: Siphon the water and oil out of the tank
Open a drain valve to remove the water and oil
The water and oil are removed automatically as the brakes are used
Use a sponge to soak up the water and oil

questions.correctAnswerText: Open a drain valve to remove the water and oil
questions.explanation: Open the drain valve to remove water and compressor oil from air storage tanks. These materials damage the brakes if they build up in the system. Manually operated tanks must be drained every day.

questions.question: What holds spring brakes in place while driving?
questions.explanation: Air pressure holds spring brakes in place while driving. If air pressure drops low enough, the springs activate the brakes.

questions.question: What is the stab braking method for an emergency stop?

options.text: Apply the brakes fully until the wheels lock up, release until the wheels roll, then repeat
Apply the brakes halfway and keep the wheels rolling
Apply the brakes fully, lock the wheels, and hold until the vehicle stops

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes fully until the wheels lock up, release until the wheels roll, then repeat
questions.explanation: The stab braking method involves applying the brakes fully until they lock up. Release the brakes until the wheels start rolling, then repeat this process.

questions.question: What should you do before driving a vehicle with a dual brake system?

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up to ensure fuel reaches the engine
Wait for the air compressor to build 100 psi in both systems
Begin driving just after the vehicle starts
Pump the pedal about 20 times to build pressure

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the air compressor to build 100 psi in both systems
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air system, wait for the air compressor to build a minimum pressure of 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: What does a one-way check valve do?

options.text: Drains water and compressor oil from the air tanks
Prevents air from escaping if the air compressor leaks
Activates the emergency brakes when there is a leak
Holds the spring brakes in position until they are used

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevents air from escaping if the air compressor leaks
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is placed between the air compressor and the first main reservoir. It prevents air from escaping the system if the air compressor develops a leak.

questions.question: How often should you drain manually operated air tanks?
questions.explanation: Drain manually operated air tanks at the end of each day of driving to prevent oil and water buildup.

questions.question: What must truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 have?
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 must have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS).

questions.question: What are truck tractors with air brakes built after March 1, 1997 equipped with?
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 are required to have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS). Other vehicles with air brakes built after March 1, 1998 also require ABS.

questions.question: What must you do before inspecting slack adjusters on S-cam brakes?

options.text: Park on a hill and test the brakes
Put on gloves and push in the slack adjusters
Remove the drum and look inside
Chock the wheels and disengage the parking brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Chock the wheels and disengage the parking brake
questions.explanation: Park on level ground, set wheel chocks, and disengage the parking brake. Pull each slack adjuster to check that it moves no more than about one inch from where the push rod attaches. If it moves more than one inch, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: On a truck with air brakes, what does the air compressor do?

options.text: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
Moves air to the back of the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pumps air into the air storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks. A device called the governor controls the air compressor.

questions.question: How many air storage tanks does an air brake system have?
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks hold compressed air. Different vehicles have different numbers and sizes of air tanks in their brake systems.

questions.question: When using controlled braking in an emergency, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Apply the brakes with about half your normal force.
Apply the brakes until the wheels lock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means pressing the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. Make small steering movements when using this method.

questions.question: When should you test the low pressure warning signal?
questions.explanation: Test your low pressure warning light before every trip to make sure it works. Let the system build up air pressure first. Then quickly press and release the brake pedal several times. This releases air from the system. The warning signal should turn on when pressure gets too low.

questions.question: What should you do before driving down a hill?
questions.explanation: Before driving down a hill, shift into a low gear. Gravity will pull your vehicle faster as you go downhill.
